featured_reviews.name: Pratyush Mohapatra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Being someone who appreciates good, genuine food created by hardworking, passionate folks - this hawker style offering came to my attention post reading some rave hidden gem reviews by the likes of prominent online portals which made me travel from Chembur just to taste this and experience.

Reaching on time is of utmost importance as they serve limited periods over lunch and dinner. Here is my honest opinion:

1. Hygiene - Fresh, neat and clean as expected from an ex hotelier

2. Value for money - Yes. A wholesome serving of half plate chicken biryani would be at INR 80 while a full plate serving of the same is at INR 150 with a tiny portion of raita which is negligible

3. Flavor - Nothing exceptional but true to basic Biryani options you would find around the city but prepared by Mr. Parkar and his parents diligently

4. Overall - A one time visit is ideal if you are in Dadar but travelling especially for this is not recommended

I think this one has caught the online hype Machine bug really well.

Our table for two orderd two pallonji sodas. As a first times pallonji taster, i liked the ice cream soda more than the popular raspberry one - it just tasted like crocin syrup.

Post hand-washing break, we dig into the pav and took turns at tasting both delicacies. I liked the Rajani Omelette more because it was spicy.

Boyfie enjoyed both but maybe he liked the kheema better. Spoiler alert: Double decker stands for two sunny side-ups on top of the kheema.

Overall, the experience was windy, tasty, unhygienic (unclean water and long hair in the kheema), fun (the owner/cashier pulls good banter). 7/10. Enjoyyyyy

featured_reviews.name: Kaustubh Havanur
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best places for pure vegetarian food. This place is easily accessible as it is located right on the main road near Sena Bhavan. You can get down at Dadar Metro Station, and as soon as you come onto the main road, the restaurant is right beside it.

Whenever you visit, you will almost always find a rush here. The waiting time can range from 30 minutes to even 1 hour. However, they have now expanded their seating capacity, and there is also a lift available to reach the first floor.

The place is also very reasonably priced. We were a group of four friends and ordered around 7–8 items, yet the total bill was only around ₹1200.

You will find a wide variety of Maharashtrian dishes here, and they have also started serving some South Indian snacks.

Must try: Modak, Aamras, and Misal Pav
You can also try the Batata Vada.

Overall, it is a great place for pure vegetarian food and definitely worth visiting with friends and family.

👉 Taste:
Most dishes were flavorful and well-prepared. The Puran Poli stood out – soft, perfectly sweet, and very satisfying. The Kothimbir Vadi was crispy and nicely spiced. The Seasonal Thali gave a good variety and felt wholesome.
👉 Quantity & Quality:
Portion sizes are decent, and ingredients taste fresh. It gives a proper “ghar jaisa khaana” vibe.
👉 Service & Waiting Time:
Had to wait around 40 minutes, which is quite long. The place gets very crowded, especially during peak hours.

Simple, traditional setup. Nothing fancy, but clean and functional. Seating can feel a bit cramped during rush hours.

After a thorough scrutiny of the menu, we ordered pithla bhakri and a chaitra thali.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.

If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!

The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Malhar recently for lunch and ordered a variety of dishes, including Crab Lollipop, Prawns Koliwada, White Rice, Rava Bombil, and Agri-style Chicken Curry. We had also planned to try Amboli and Bhakri, but unfortunately, both were out of stock.

The Crab Lollipop and Prawns Koliwada were flavorful and well-prepared. However, the Agri-style Chicken Curry did not meet expectations. The use of garam masala was overpowering, and the excessive black pepper (kalimiri) affected the overall taste, though the dish was still edible.

The ambience of the restaurant was very beautiful, but I noticed some issues with cleanliness. For example, one of the glasses provided still had food particles stuck on the edge where a person drinks. I requested the steward to replace the glass; he took the dirty one but forgot to bring a new glass altogether, leaving me to drink directly from the bottle.

While the food was average overall, I was particularly disappointed with the service. Both the steward and the captain seemed uninterested and inattentive. Despite repeated requests, it took them over 15 minutes to bring tissues, even when asked clearly and politely.

Additionally, the Prawns Koliwada was served nearly 40 minutes later, after we had almost finished our main course. At that time, only 3–4 tables were occupied in the restaurant, so such a delay was unjustified. When I raised this issue with the captain, his casual response was, "Humare yaha thoda late hi hota hai." This type of attitude is not expected from a reputed establishment like Malhar.

In summary, although the ambience was nice and some dishes were good, the poor service, lack of attention to cleanliness, and indifferent staff attitude significantly impacted our overall dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
### Apoorva: A Hidden Gem for Delicious Vegetarian Delights

If you’re searching for a restaurant in Dadar that delivers more than just satisfying food, look no further than **Apoorva**. This pure veg family restaurant, nestled in the heart of Dadar, is a culinary haven for those who appreciate authentic Maharashtrian, South Indian, North Indian, and Desi Chinese cuisine—all served with a generous side of flavor and quality.

#### **Food Quality and Taste: A Delightful Surprise**
The moment you take your first bite at Apoorva, you’ll understand why it’s a local favorite. The food quality here is impeccable, from the freshest ingredients to the skilled preparation. Every dish, whether it’s the spicy Pav Bhaji, the creamy Butter Paneer  Masala, the crisp and savory Dosas, or the perfectly spiced Hakka Noodles, bursts with authentic flavors. The South Indian offerings, in particular, are a standout, with sambar that tastes like it’s straight out of a traditional kitchen and dosas that are golden, crispy, and oh-so-satisfying.

Apoorva has mastered the art of balancing taste with health, ensuring that the food is not just tasty but also light on the stomach, making it ideal for regular visits. Whether you’re a local or a visitor, the varied menu has something to please every palate.

Ambiance: Choices for Every Mood.
Apoorva offers three distinct seating options, catering to different preferences:
1. **Roadside Open Seats**: Perfect for those who enjoy dining al fresco, these seats give you a lively view of the bustling streets of Dadar. It's a great choice if you love people-watching while enjoying your meal. I love sitting here during Monsoon.
2. **Non-AC Inside Restaurant**: For a more traditional dining experience, the non-AC section offers a cozy, no-frills environment where you can focus on the food and conversation.
3. **AC Seats Inside Restaurant**: If you’re looking to beat the heat, the AC section provides a comfortable and cool respite from the Mumbai sun.

However, the seating area here can feel a bit cramped, so it’s best for smaller groups.

While the ambiance is simple and straightforward, it’s the food that truly shines at Apoorva. The seating might be cumbersome, especially during peak hours, but the culinary experience more than makes up for it.

**Parking: A Word of Caution**
One thing to note: if you’re planning to drive, parking can be a challenge. Roadside parking is notoriously difficult in this busy area, so it’s wise to avoid bringing a car if possible. Opt for public transport or a quick Taxi ride to save yourself the hassle.

**Location: A Convenient Spot in Dadar**
Apoorva’s location is another big plus. Situated close to major landmarks like Shivaji Park, Dadar Beach, Sushrusha Hospital, and Ranade Road, it’s easily accessible whether you’re out for a stroll, visiting a friend, or just exploring the neighborhood. Despite being in such a prime area, Apoorva maintains its reputation as one of the best budget-friendly restaurants around.

**Final Thoughts**
Apoorva is more than just a restaurant; it’s a place where food lovers come together to enjoy hearty, flavorful meals without breaking the bank. The quality, taste, and variety of the food make it a must-visit for anyone in Dadar, especially if you’re looking for a budget-friendly option that doesn’t compromise on flavor. Whether you’re in the mood for a quick snack or a full meal, Apoorva is ready to serve you with warmth and authenticity.

Next time you’re in Dadar, don’t miss the chance to dine at Apoorva—you’ll leave with a full stomach and a happy heart.

featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Primarily, a delivery outlet Charcoal eats serve awesome quick bites to munch on as late as 3 am during weekends and till 11 pm during weekdays. The place has seating arrangements too which I assume that hardly anybody show up for dine in whereas like most of us opt for delivery service from the outlet. It offers amazing biryanis and quick bites as the brand says it all - 'bite that good' and yes we do bite it good from Charcoal Eats. The delivery is outstanding with organised colourful packaging. I happened to go on for trying out their famous biryani and some quick bites right at their outlet in Dadar east. I found the interiors very attractive and cosy. Since the place has famed itself more into delivery but otheriwse I think it is also a chill place to dine in with family and friends.
Talking about my yummilicious orders, I had-
1) Peach Ice Tea - They serve beautiful glass bottles of 'Brewhouse' Peach Ice Tea. Its cute as well as amazing drink to opt for with the meal aside.
2) Barbeque Loaded Fries- Crispy potato fried topped with bbq sauce and some spicy masala were tasting too good when eaten hot.
3) Chicken Mughlai Paratha- Chicken chunks and onion mixture loaded inside fried parathas tasted just like the rolls.
4) Chicken Tikka Biryani- Reasonable price for the awesome biryani. Small chicken chunks beneath the fine layered biryani can be good to go to try this one.
5) Salted Caramel Mousse- The salty and sweet taste of this chocolate mousse is divine. Although not their in house production, but still this one would be loved be loved by all the sweet lovers just like me.
I totally loved this vibrant place. And it serves awesome quick bites and biryanis and moreover at decent price that could be the relevant reason for quick hogging to opt for from the same.

A must-visit landmark for anyone who appreciates quality, tradition, and genuine taste.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had heard a lot about Gomantak in Dadar. On my recent visit, I finally decided to try it. It was raining heavily that day. Even then, the restaurant was completely packed. They have both AC and non-AC sections. I had to wait for about 15 to 20 minutes before getting a table. The crowd itself gave me a sense of how popular this place is among seafood lovers.

I ordered the Chicken Masala Thali and Crab Masala with Rice Bhakri. The Chicken Masala Thali came with Chicken Gravy, Chicken Rassa, Rice, Bhakri, Sol Kadi, and Salad. The Chicken Gravy had a rich flavour that reminded me of coastal Goan cooking. It had depth, warmth, and a balance of spice. The Chicken Rassa was light and paired beautifully with rice. The Sol Kadi worked as a refreshing sip after the gravies.

The Crab Masala was the highlight of the meal. The crab meat was fresh and sweet. The masala was layered with flavour and had the right amount of spice. The meat absorbed the masala so well that every bite felt satisfying. The staff even help you break the crab if needed, which makes it easier to enjoy. The Rice Bhakri was soft and thick. It soaked up the masala and gravies perfectly.

To finish, I ordered the Caramel Custard. It was smooth, light, and mildly sweet. It balanced the spice of the seafood dishes.

Gomantak is a family-style restaurant that focuses on good food rather than frills. The service was courteous and attentive. The prices are fair for the portions and quality. It is a reliable place in Dadar if you are looking for seafood that feels authentic and comforting.

Ratings:
Quality – 4/5
Quantity – 4.1/5
Service – 4/5
Price – ₹800 for 2 people
